# Settings

Settings live in `~/.config/termocode/config.json` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/termocode/config.json`). Change them with **Preferences: Open Settings (UI)**, or edit the file by hand. A missing key uses its default. Unknown keys are kept.

```json
{
  "theme": "vscode-dark-plus",
  "tab_size": 4,
  "word_wrap": true
}
```

## Appearance

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `theme` | string | `vscode-dark-plus` | Color theme ID. Same as Preferences: Color Theme. |
| `icons` | enum | `auto` | Icon set: nerd (Nerd Font glyphs), unicode (plain symbols), ascii, or auto (nerd when the terminal bundles Nerd symbols — WezTerm, Ghostty, kitty — or its font setting is a Nerd Font — GNOME Terminal profile, Alacritty, foot; ascii on TERM=linux or a non-UTF-8 locale; else unicode). TERMOCODE_ICON_MODE wins over it. |
| `animations` | enum | `auto` | Overlay / toast / list animations: on, off, or auto (off over SSH and when the terminal is not truecolor). The editor text itself never animates. |
| `images` | enum | `auto` | Inline images (image preview, dashboard logo, Markdown preview): kitty, sixel, blocks (coloured half-blocks, works everywhere with colour), off, or auto (probe the terminal; blocks inside tmux without allow-passthrough). |
| `dashboard_logo` | enum | `text` | The TERMOCODE wordmark on the Welcome page: text (half-blocks, works everywhere), image (a kitty / sixel picture; needs images on), or off. A short window shows a one-line text wordmark instead, so the page fits. |
| `font_delta` | int | `0` | Font size change (points) asked of the terminal at launch and undone on exit; 0 turns it off. Works only in kitty with allow_remote_control on; other terminals (iTerm2, WezTerm, Ghostty, GNOME, Windows Terminal …) have no way to do it, so use their zoom (Ctrl+-). TERMOCODE_FONT_DELTA wins over it. |

## Editor

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auto_save` | bool | `false` | Save files automatically after edits. |
| `word_wrap` | bool | `false` | Soft-wrap long lines in the editor. |
| `show_hidden` | bool | `false` | Show dot-files in the explorer. |
| `key_hints` | bool | `true` | Show a small popup of the next keys when you press the leader key in the editor and wait a moment. Esc closes it. |
| `tab_size` | int | `4` | Indent width in spaces (1-16). Sets tabstop and shiftwidth. |
| `persistent_session` | enum | `auto` | Run the editor in a background session that survives a dropped connection; run termocode again in the same folder to get it back: on, off, or auto (on over SSH, off locally and inside tmux / screen). Applies the next time termocode starts; --no-session wins over it. |
| `auto_reconnect` | bool | `true` | When the connection to a persistent session drops (network change, Wi-Fi switch, sleep), keep the screen and attach again by itself, also after `termocode ssh` restarts ssh. Keys typed while offline are not sent. Applies the next time termocode starts. |

## Search

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `search_max_results` | int | `2000` | Most results Find in Files shows. 0 means no limit. |

## AI

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ai_inline` | bool | `true` | Show AI ghost-text completions while typing (needs a configured provider). |
| `ai_next_edit` | bool | `true` | After an edit, show where the AI thinks the next related edit goes (Tab: go there, Tab: apply, Esc: dismiss). Not set: same as ai_inline. |
| `ai_provider` | string | `(auto)` | AI provider: anthropic, openai, openrouter, ollama, lmstudio, openai-compatible, claude-oauth or none. Empty picks anthropic or openai from the API keys it finds. TERMOCODE_AI_PROVIDER overrides it. |
| `ai_model` | string | `(default)` | Chat model ID. Empty uses the provider's default model. |
| `ai_base_url` | string | `(default)` | API base URL, for local or OpenAI-compatible servers. Empty uses the provider's default. |
| `ai_until_done_rounds` | int | `3` | Work until done (the until-done profile, /done, AI: Work Until Done): how many times verify runs at most (1 to 10). A profile's loop.max_rounds wins over it. |
| `ai_until_done_budget_usd` | number | `2.00` | Work until done: the run pauses and asks once its steps have cost this many US dollars. 0 means no budget. A profile's budget_usd wins over it. |

## HTTP

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `http_timeout` | int | `30` | Seconds an HTTP request may take (from .http files, Quick Request and the AI's http_send); # @timeout in a request wins. |
| `http_max_redirects` | int | `10` | Most redirects an HTTP request follows; # @no-redirect in a request shows the 3xx itself. |
| `http_max_body_mb` | int | `20` | Largest HTTP response body read, in MB; a bigger one is cut and marked truncated. |
| `http_ai_max_kb` | int | `32` | Most KB of a response body the AI sees per http_send / http_get_last_response call (it can page on with offset). |
| `http_tls_insecure` | bool | `false` | Skip TLS certificate checks for your own HTTP requests (never for the AI's). Prefer the k retry on the response page, which is per host and per session. |
| `http_cookie_jar` | bool | `true` | Keep cookies between HTTP requests (in memory only, per session); # @no-cookie-jar in a request turns it off for that request. |
| `http_history_max` | int | `200` | Most entries kept in http/history.jsonl. |

## MCP

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mcp_enabled` | bool | `true` | Offer the tools of the MCP servers in mcp.json to the AI chat. false hides them all without touching mcp.json. |
| `mcp_idle_timeout` | string | `10m` | Stop an MCP server after this long without a tool call (a local one ends, a remote one drops its session); it starts again on the next call. "0" never stops it. A Go duration: 90s, 10m, 1h. |
| `mcp_call_timeout` | string | `60s` | Longest wait for one MCP tool call without an answer or a progress report. A server's "timeout" (seconds) in mcp.json wins. |
| `mcp_max_result_kb` | int | `32` | Cut an MCP tool result to this many KB before the model sees it. |
| `mcp_trust_annotations` | bool | `true` | Let MCP tools the server marks read-only run without asking. false: every MCP tool asks, except the ones in the server's "autoApprove" list. |
| `mcp_oauth_port` | int | `0` | Port of the sign-in listener on 127.0.0.1 for MCP servers with OAuth. 0 takes the first free one of 47391–47395 (the ports termocode's client document lists, so ssh -L 47391:127.0.0.1:47391 works); set another only for an app registered with that port. |
| `mcp_github_client_id` | string | `(built in)` | Client ID of a GitHub OAuth App with Device Flow on, for the GitHub sign-in with a code (Connect a service). Empty uses the one built into termocode (none until it is registered). Not a secret. |
| `mcp_share` | bool | `true` | Run each local MCP server once for all your termocode windows with the same server entry and folder, not once per window. It ends when the last window stops using it (mcp_idle_timeout or quit). false: every window runs its own. Remote servers are not affected. |
| `mcp_tool_search` | string | `auto` | Send the AI only a search tool instead of every MCP tool's full schema; it loads the tools it needs. auto: only when the MCP tools are big (about 10k tokens). on: always. off: never. |
| `mcp_catalog_url` | string |   | Catalog that AI: MCP: Browse Catalog… reads (an MCP Registry API, for example your team's approved list). Empty: the official MCP Registry. Must be https. |

## Updates

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `update_check` | bool | `true` | Look for a newer termocode release once a day, in the background (GitHub, no account needed). A newer one shows a quiet ⬆ chip in the status bar and one toast. Dev builds never look. termocode: Check for Updates works with it off too. |

## Databases (file only)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `db_max_rows` | int | `10000` | Maximum loaded rows per SQL result (1–100000). Larger results are cut and marked. |
| `db_page_rows` | int | `100` | Rows per SQL result page (1–1000). |
| `db_timeout` | int | `30` | Maximum seconds for a console statement. The session also enforces its own timeout. |
| `db_history_max` | int | `500` | Maximum SQL history entries kept in db/history.jsonl. |
| `db_ai_max_kb` | int | `32` | Maximum size in KB of one AI database tool answer (1–1024). Longer results are cut and marked. |
| `db_redis_separator` | string | `:` | Separator that groups Redis keys into namespaces in the tree (session:ab12 is under session:). Empty: no grouping. |
| `db_redis_max_keys` | int | `10000` | Most Redis keys one tree row loads with SCAN (100–1000000). Past it the row says so; open a namespace to see more. |

## Containers (file only)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `containers_engine` | enum | `auto` | Container engine of the Containers view. auto tries Docker, then Podman; docker or podman uses only that engine. Press R in the view after changing it. |
| `containers_sections` | string[] | `all` | Sections shown by the Containers view, across workspaces. The Containers menu writes this list; collapse state is kept in the workspace session. |
| `containers_max_inspect_kb` | int | `64` | Cut the JSON the AI's containers_inspect tool returns to this many KB. Env values, auth fields and secret-looking labels are masked before the cut. |

## AI (file only)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ai_inline_model` | string | `(provider default)` | Model for inline ghost-text completions. Empty uses a fast model of the provider (for example Claude Haiku or gpt-4.1-mini). |
| `ai_auto_approve` | string[] | `[]` | Agent tool classes that run without asking: fileWrite, git, run, ide, settings, services. Set with AI: Agent Auto-Approve…. |
| `ai_edit_review` | enum | `review` | review: the agent's file changes (write_file, create_file, LSP rename, code actions, format) open as a diff where you accept or reject each change; the agent waits and is told what was written. auto: the old way (a confirm dialog, or no question when fileWrite is auto-approved). Auto-approving fileWrite also skips the review. Toggle with AI: Toggle Edit Review. |
| `ai_max_steps` | int | `25` | Most tool steps the AI agent takes for one chat message. At the limit it stops and asks you to send "continue". |
| `ai_prices` | object | `{}` | Model prices in US dollars per million tokens, by model id prefix, over the built-in table (checked 2026-10-18): for example `{"my-model": {"in": 3, "out": 15, "cache_read": 0.3, "cache_write": 3.75}}`. A missing cache price is the input price. Your entry wins over a built-in one. Ollama and LM Studio cost $0; a model with no price shows tokens only. |
| `ai_context_windows` | object | `{}` | Context window in tokens, by model id prefix, over the built-in table: for example `{"qwen2.5-coder": 32768}`. Used for the context % of a turn; a model with no window shows none. |
| `ai_models` | object | `{}` | Model slots for agent profiles (ai/profiles.json): slot name → `{"provider", "model", "base_url"}`, for example `{"gpt": {"provider": "openai", "model": "gpt-5-mini"}}`. No keys here: a slot uses the key of its provider kind (environment variable, then AI: Configure Provider…). Built-in slots: `main` (ai_provider / ai_model, can not be replaced), `quick` (the main provider with ai_inline_model) and `local` (Ollama); a slot with the name quick or local replaces the built-in one. A bad entry is left out and named in the profile errors. |
| `ai_parallel_max` | int | `1` | How many steps of an agent profile may run at the same time (at most 8). With 1, steps run one after the other and profiles may not use `deps`. When it is not set, a planned run (a profile with a `plan` step, like the built-in plan profile) runs up to 3 steps at once. |
| `ai_worktrees` | enum | `auto` | auto: in a git repository, each agent step that runs at the same time as another writing step works in its own git worktree (branch termocode/agent-<id>), so they never change the same files. When it ends, its card shows the changed files with Review, Merge and Discard. off: every step works in your tree. Toggle with AI: Toggle Agent Worktrees. |
| `ai_plan_approval` | enum | `ask` | ask: before an agent run starts a step that changes files or runs commands, the chat shows the plan (steps, models, budget) with Deny, Approve and Edit; a read-only plan runs at once. auto: plans run without asking. always: every plan asks, read-only ones too. AI: Toggle Plan Approval turns it on or off for one chat. |
| `secret_store` | enum | `auto` | Where AI keys, sign-ins, MCP secrets and database passwords are kept. auto: the OS keyring when one answers (not over SSH, not on Termux), else an encrypted file (secrets.age, a passphrase asked once while termocode runs); never the plain file. keyring or age uses only that one (keyring with no keyring is an error, not a fallback). plain: the old ai/credentials.json (mode 0600), by choice only. An existing plain ai/credentials.json stays in use under auto until you move it (the card at start, or AI: Move Secrets to a Safer Store…). The choice is recorded in secrets.json. |
| `secret_lock_minutes` | int | `0` | Lock the encrypted secret file after this many idle minutes (0 = never; the passphrase stays until AI: Lock Secrets or quit). Each use of a secret starts the count again. Only while the file is unlocked does one timer run; none with 0, for the OS keyring or for the plain file. Read when the file is unlocked. |
| `mcp_trusted` | object | `{}` | Project MCP servers you allowed with "Always allow": server name → hash of its mcp.json entry. A changed entry asks again. Written by the trust dialog and AI: MCP Servers…. |
| `mcp_server` | enum | `auto` | termocode as an MCP server: outside agents (Claude Code, Codex, …) reach a short list of IDE tools (open files, diagnostics, tests, debugger, terminal and git reads) over a private socket in the session folder, open only to your own user. Tools that change something ask on a card first; files, settings, git writes and your own MCP servers are never offered. auto: serve once you start an agent tab (F1 → Agent: Start …). on: serve from start. off: never. Applied when you save config.json. |
| `mcp_server_auto_approve` | object | `{}` | The "Always allow" answers you gave on an outside agent's card (see mcp_server): agent name → tool names that run without asking for that agent. Separate from ai_auto_approve, which never applies to outside agents. The name is the agent's own claim. See and revoke them in AI: Agent Auto-Approve…. |
| `mcp_trusted_tools` | object | `{}` | The tool list you trusted per MCP server: server name → hash of its tools. The first list is kept by itself; when a server's tools change, termocode asks again and, until you trust the new list, every tool of that server asks first. |

## Services (file only)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `services_on_quit` | enum | `ask` | On quit, the Docker Compose services termocode started in this session (never the ones that were already running): ask shows a card (Keep running and quit / Stop and quit / Cancel), keep leaves them running, stop runs docker compose stop for them first. Local services always stop with the editor. |
| `services_max_log_kb` | int | `16` | Cut the log text the AI's services_logs tool returns to this many KB (the newest lines stay). |

## Web (file only)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `web_panel` | enum | `off` | The web panel (experimental): your files, chats and terminals in a web browser, on this computer or over SSH. on: termocode listens on a private socket in the session folder, and Web: Start Panel (or termocode web) can open the panel after you say yes on a card. Anyone who controls the browser tab can run any command as you. off: nothing listens and the commands only explain how to turn it on. Applied when you save config.json. |
| `web_listen` | enum | `loopback` | Where the web panel can be reached. loopback: only on this computer (127.0.0.1), or over termocode ssh --web. tailnet: also from your own devices on your Tailscale network, at https://<this computer>.<tailnet>.ts.net/; termocode runs tailscale serve while the panel runs and refuses to start when the port is public (Funnel). Needs Tailscale with HTTPS turned on. |
| `web_require_totp` | bool | `false` | A paired phone or tablet also types a 6-digit code from an authenticator app after its passkey. Set the code up first with Web: Set Up Sign-in Code… (its key is kept in your secret store, which must be unlocked when a device signs in). The one-time link from this computer does not need it. |
| `web_port` | int | `0` | The port the web panel listens on, on 127.0.0.1 only. 0: a free port each time. Else 1024..65535. |
| `web_idle_minutes` | int | `15` | The web panel stops after this many minutes with no use from any browser (1..120). |
| `web_max_hours` | int | `12` | The web panel stops this many hours after it started, in use or not (1..24). |
| `web_open_browser` | bool | `true` | Open the one-time link in the browser of this computer when the panel starts. false: only Copy link on the start card or Web: Copy Link. |
| `web_max_viewers` | int | `4` | How many browsers may be connected at once (1..8). One more is turned away. |

## Appearance (file only)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mouse_hover` | enum | `auto` | auto: the terminal reports plain pointer motion (xterm mode 1003) while termocode has focus and no text input is open, for hover labels and row highlights. off: only clicks, drags and the wheel (mode 1002), for terminals or links where motion is slow or dropped. Read at start. |
| `rtl` | enum | `auto` | Right-to-left text (Persian, Arabic, Hebrew) in the AI chat and the Markdown preview. termocode: termocode joins the letters and puts them in reading order itself, right-aligns RTL paragraphs, and asks the terminal not to reorder (BDSM, CSI 8 l). terminal: termocode sends the text unchanged and the terminal does it. off: unchanged text, no request to the terminal. auto: terminal on Konsole and mlterm (they always reorder), else termocode. Read at start. |

## Terminal (file only)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `terminal_skip_shell` | string[] | `[]` | Actions (keymap.json names) whose keys reach termocode while the terminal has focus. Other Ctrl keys go to the shell. Quit (Ctrl+Q) and ContextHelp (Shift+F1) are in the list by default; add a name, or remove one with "-Name" (for example `["QuickOpen", "-Quit"]`). |
| `terminal_restore` | bool | `true` | After a restart of termocode, the terminal tabs of the project come back: each tab and split pane gets a fresh shell in the folder it was in, and the same tab and pane have focus. Output, scrollback and environment values are never kept. A pane that was running a program shows its name. A folder that is gone starts in the project folder. false: the panel starts empty. Read at start. |
| `terminal_restore_commands` | bool | `false` | With terminal_restore: also keep the last command line of a pane that was running a program (needs shell integration), so after a restart Enter in that pane runs it again. Command lines can hold secrets, so this is off by default; off, only the program name is kept. Read at start. |
| `terminal_shell_integration` | bool | `true` | bash, zsh and fish terminal tabs load a small script (after your own rc file) that tells termocode each command, its exit code and the folder (OSC 133 / OSC 7). It gives the tab its folder name, the "✦ Fix?" chip on a failed command and the CLI agent marks. false starts the shell exactly as before. Read when a terminal tab opens; needs Neovim 0.10+. |

## Environment variables

| Variable | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Anthropic API key. Also selects Anthropic when no provider is set. |
| `OLLAMA_HOST` | Ollama host, used for the base URL of the ollama provider. |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | OpenAI API key. Also selects OpenAI when no provider is set. |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | OpenRouter API key. |
| `TERMOCODE_AI_API_KEY` | AI API key for the selected provider; wins over saved keys. |
| `TERMOCODE_AI_BASE_URL` | AI API base URL; wins over `ai_base_url`. |
| `TERMOCODE_AI_MODEL` | AI chat model; wins over `ai_model`. |
| `TERMOCODE_AI_PROVIDER` | AI provider; wins over `ai_provider` in config.json. |
| `TERMOCODE_FONT_DELTA` | Font size change asked of the terminal at launch (kitty with remote control only); wins over font_delta in config.json (default 0 = off). |
| `TERMOCODE_FRAME_PACING` | on / off: wait for the terminal before sending more frames, so a held key stops at once on a slow line (default: on over SSH). |
| `TERMOCODE_ICON_MODE` | Icon set: `nerd_font`, `unicode` or `ascii`. |
| `TERMOCODE_NERD_FONT` | Legacy: `1` is the same as `TERMOCODE_ICON_MODE=nerd_font`. |
| `TERMOCODE_NO_SESSION` | Any value: run without a persistent session, like `--no-session`. |
| `TERMOCODE_PLUGINS_DIR` | Folder for the Neovim plugins termocode clones on first launch. |
| `TERMOCODE_PROBE` | `off`: never ask the terminal what it can do at start (images, cell size, kitty keyboard); the environment decides. A terminal that did not answer is not asked again for 7 days (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/termocode/termcaps.json`). |
| `TERMOCODE_SYNC` | on / off: draw each frame as one (synchronized output, mode 2026), so no half-drawn frame shows on a slow link (default: on when the terminal says it supports it). |
| `TERMOCODE_TOOLS_DIR` | Folder for language servers and debug adapters installed by termocode. |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | Moves the config folder to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/termocode`. |
| `XDG_DATA_HOME` | Moves the data folder to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/termocode`. |
| `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` | Folder for the persistent-session sockets (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/termocode`); without it they go to `~/.cache/termocode/sessions`. |
| `XDG_STATE_HOME` | Moves the hot-exit backups of unsaved files to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/termocode/backup`. |
